deliverables.name: Data Ingestion Connectors (Jira + GitHub)
deliverables.description: Ingestion layer that pulls issue and commit history from Arclight's Jira and GitHub organizations into Continuity, including incremental sync, webhook-driven updates, and historical backfill.
deliverables.acceptance: Jira issues and GitHub commits/PRs sync within 5 minutes of a change; full historical backfill completes without manual intervention; webhook delivery survives bursts of 50+ events/minute without dropped updates; attachment metadata ingests without silent failures.
excludes: Connectors for any source control or issue tracker other than Jira and GitHub
Real-time/streaming ingestion (sub-minute latency)
Migrating or archiving Arclight's data out of Jira/GitHub

deliverables.name: Ticket-to-Commit Linkage & Coverage Reporting
deliverables.description: Automatic association of GitHub commits/PRs with the Jira tickets they implement, plus a coverage report showing what percentage of tickets have linked code.
deliverables.acceptance: Commit messages referencing a ticket key in any of Arclight's existing formatting conventions are correctly linked; coverage report updates as new commits land; a ticket linking to multiple commits is not double-counted.
excludes: Sprint velocity, burndown, or estimation-accuracy reporting
Linking tickets across more than one Jira instance
Automatically closing or transitioning Jira tickets based on commit/PR activity

deliverables.name: Hybrid Search & Cited Q&A
deliverables.description: Retrieval system over Arclight's ingested project data supporting natural-language questions with citations back to the source ticket or commit.
deliverables.acceptance: Queries combine keyword and semantic search; every answer includes at least one clickable citation; retrieval latency under 2s p95 up to 200k indexed chunks; system abstains rather than fabricates when unsupported.
excludes: Multi-language translation of source content or answers
A conversational voice interface
Generating or submitting code changes on Arclight's behalf

deliverables.name: Handover Brief & Work-State Assembly
deliverables.description: Automatic assembly of a handover brief for any engineer — open tickets, open PRs, unmerged branches, recent commit activity — without requiring the person to self-report.
deliverables.acceptance: Brief reflects live Jira/GitHub state at generation time; correctly shows PRs awaiting review from other people, not just the subject's own; requires no action from the departing engineer.
excludes: Any performance, velocity, or productivity scoring of individuals
HR or org-chart data (reporting lines, compensation, review history)
Automated reassignment of tickets or PRs

deliverables.name: Scope Guardian — SOW Parsing & Classification
deliverables.description: Parses an uploaded Statement of Work into structured deliverables and acceptance criteria, then classifies incoming tickets as in-scope, out-of-scope, or ambiguous against it.
deliverables.acceptance: SOW upload produces an editable deliverable list for PM confirmation; tickets are classified with a stated reason; a written, consistent definition of ambiguous vs. out-of-scope is applied.
excludes: Legal review or redlining of the SOW document itself
Automatic ticket rejection or closure based on classification
Classifying scope for engagements without a parseable SOW on file

deliverables.name: Provenance & Read-Time Permission Evaluation
deliverables.description: Tracks the source of every retrieved piece of information and evaluates read access at query time, including immediately after access is revoked.
deliverables.acceptance: Every citation traces back to its exact source record; a user whose access is revoked loses read access on their next query without a cache flush or restart; row-level security enforced on all citation-facing tables.
excludes: Building or replacing Arclight's identity provider / SSO system
Formal compliance certification (SOC 2, ISO 27001, etc.)
Write-access permissions or approval workflows

deliverables.name: Secrets Scanning & Canary Tokens
deliverables.description: Scans ingested commit history for leaked credentials before indexing, and embeds canary tokens in seeded/test content to detect unauthorized access or exfiltration.
deliverables.acceptance: Common secret patterns are detected before content reaches the searchable index; canary token triggers reliably fire alerts, including when the alerting webhook is briefly unreachable; false positives on legitimate fixtures are minimized.
excludes: Automatically rotating, revoking, or remediating a discovered secret
Scanning artifact stores or secrets managers outside ingested Git history
Guaranteeing detection of novel or custom secret formats

deliverables.name: Auto-Draft from PRs — Assisted Capture
deliverables.description: When a PR is merged, automatically drafts a knowledge-base note summarizing the change and its reasoning, pending human review and approval before publishing.
deliverables.acceptance: A draft is generated per qualifying merged PR without author effort; drafts sit pending until explicitly approved; approved notes are searchable through D3 with correct provenance to the source PR.
excludes: Auto-publishing a draft without human approval
Drafting for repositories or PRs outside Arclight's connected GitHub organization
Translating drafts into languages other than English

out_of_scope_tickets.reason: Violates D7 exclusion: automatically rotating, revoking, or remediating a discovered secret.
Not part of any contracted deliverable (D1-D8) — billing/subscription management is unrelated to Continuity's scope.
D3 covers a text-based Q&A surface but doesn't specify whether that extends to a new channel integration like Slack — a stretch fit, not clean in-scope or out-of-scope.
